title: What it's called
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The print tech asks what the digest is called. It's called the digest. He means the strip. The strip is called Drift Wood. He asks why. Wood has never been asked.

panels.composition: The print shop. The machine warming. The TECH in the apron with a strip up to the light. WOOD waiting.

image.prompt: a print shop technician in an apron holding a comic strip up to the light while a young man waits beside a large photocopier, black and white, no words
a young man's face caught off guard, mouth slightly open, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood looking at the copier's green light sweeping. A long panel for a short question.

image.prompt: a young man watching the green light of a photocopier sweep under its lid, thinking, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The tech stacking copies. Wood, finally.

balloons.text: Huh. Thought it was your name.

image.prompt: a technician stacking warm photocopies while a young man answers, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: First time anyone asks. 'Thought it was your name.' It is.
